content: Jacqui Jackson is a single mother raising seven children, consisting of three adolescent daughters and four sons. All four of her sons are on the autism spectrum. In 2003, Jackson and her family were featured in a BBC documentary titled My Family and Autism. Later, in 2005, BBC Two aired a drama called Magnificent 7, in which Helena Bonham Carter portrayed a character named Maggi, who was based on Jacqui Jackson. Jackson resides in Blackpool, Lancashire, England. Her sons include: Matthew, the eldest child in the family, who was born prematurely. He has been diagnosed with dyslexia and developmental dyspraxia. Luke, who has been diagnosed with Asperger syndrome and dyspraxia. At the age of 13, Luke authored a book titled Freaks, Geeks and Asperger's Syndrome, which details his experiences living with the condition. Joe, who has been diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). Ben, the youngest child in the family, who was also born prematurely and is autistic. In addition to her sons, Jackson has three daughters named Rachel, Sarah, and Anna. Jacqui Jackson holds a first-class honours degree in social science from the Open University. She is currently pursuing a PhD at Coventry University, focusing on sensory issues in autistic children. She has authored the following books: Multicoloured Mayhem, published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers in 2003 (ISBN: 1-84310-171-8). Damned Hard Day: Living with AD/HD, published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers in 2005 (ISBN: 1-84310-296-X).
